newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent spikes up on gas oil but then dips back.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent spikes up on gas oil but then dips back.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures opened around unchanged but stronger gas oil futures spiked the market higher shortly after the opening, brokers said.
July Brent opened unchanged at $20.13 a barrel. An early spike to $20.22 met resistance and it eased back to trade unchanged at $20.13 a barrel at 0945 GMT.
June Gas oil opened 75 cents up, made quick $2 gains to trade at $178.25 a tonne then dipped to $177.50.
Brokers said Brent recovered well last night, partly in response to rising tension on the borders of northern Iraq and the stronger gas oil had initially provided a further boost.
Turkish troops have pushed 200 km into northern Iraq in a nine-day offensive against Kurdish guerrillas, Iraqi Kurdish officials said on Thursday.

Turkey's operation in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) separatists has unnerved its neighbours. Turkey's state-run news agency Anatolia reported Wednesday that Iraq, Syria and Iran have all built up forces in the region.

"The Turkish incursions are still causing a few jitters but basically you have two schools of thought: the fundamentalists think the market should be coming lower but then there are a lot of long funds who are happy to sit with it," said a broker.

Dealers saw interim support on Brent at $20.00 a barrel. Gas oil, meanwhile, was stuck in the middle of a $175-$180 a tonne trading range with little momentum seen for break in either direction, dealers said.
The approach of a long holiday weekend in Britain and the U.S. was expected to keep markets thin and choppy, they said.
